citation.title: AutoMS: Multi-Agent Evolutionary Search for Cross-Physics Inverse Microstructure Design
citation.authors: Zhenyuan Zhao, Yu Xing, Tianyang Xue, Lingxin Cao, Xin Yan, Lin Lu
citation.version_coded: arXiv v2 (12 Apr 2026; v1 28 Mar 2026), full text read from https://arxiv.org/html/2603.27195

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded). Headline: 83.8% success rate on 17 cross-physics tasks versus NSGA-II 43.7%, CMA-ES 66.7% and BayesOpt 65.0%, all baselines searching the inputs of the same learned MIND generator.

notes: Excluded as ML-only (PROTOCOL §4). Every baseline (NSGA-II, BayesOpt with a Gaussian-process surrogate, CMA-ES, ReAct, and the SAES variants) optimizes the conditioning vector (E, G, ν) of the same pretrained MIND diffusion generator with the same simulator (Sec. 4 Baselines; App. B.2). No TO or inverse-homogenization comparator is run; TO appears only as motivation (abstract, Introduction, Related Work). Judgment call for the verifier: the authors call NSGA-II and CMA-ES traditional numerical baselines. If generator-wrapped evolutionary search is accepted as a classical comparator, the record would enter stratum Q with primary outcome SR 83.8% vs NSGA-II 43.7% (Table 1). Table 1 also lists wall-clock times of 2180.5 s (AutoMS), 5550.2 s (NSGA-II), 4202.3 s (CMA-ES) and 3982.9 s (BayesOpt), averaged over four runs, excluding plasticity simulations (Sec. 4; App. E.3); hardware is two NVIDIA A40 GPUs and a 64-core AMD EPYC 7763 (Sec. 4). Physics: homogenized elasticity, thermal and electrical conductivity, and plasticity on 64^3 voxels with C3D8 elements and a PCG solver (App. D.3). No code availability statement found. Screening code was I-QUALITY.
